title: Museum of Manufactures established
documented_change: Created after the Great Exhibition with an explicit educational and industrial-improvement purpose.
why_it_matters: The founding logic tied collecting and display to design education, manufacturing standards and public instruction.
what_remained: The collection was already conceived as an instrument of formation, not simply a store of objects.

title: Moves to South Kensington
documented_change: The museum moves to South Kensington and becomes the South Kensington Museum.
why_it_matters: The institution becomes embedded in the larger 'Albertopolis' ecology.

title: Renamed Victoria and Albert Museum
documented_change: Queen Victoria lays the foundation stone for new buildings and the Museum is renamed.
why_it_matters: The change consolidates a national identity around art and design while its purpose is reconsidered.
what_remained: The connection between collections, design education and public refinement remains central.

title: National Heritage Act
documented_change: The Act provides the modern statutory trustee framework.
why_it_matters: Formalises the Board architecture under which trustees are appointed by the Prime Minister.
what_remained: The institution remains publicly sponsored but governed through trustees.

title: DCMS framework 2025–28
documented_change: A current framework sets out the DCMS–V&A relationship under Managing Public Money.
why_it_matters: Makes the mixture of arm's-length governance, public appointments and spending controls explicit.
what_remained: The framework does not replace statutory or charitable duties.
